common_name: Dwarf Singapore Pink Plumeria (Compact Fragrant Pink Frangipani)

planting.note: Allow cuttings to dry and callus for 1-2 weeks before planting in extremely well-drained, sandy soil in full sun; this compact, evergreen-leaning selection stays smaller than typical deciduous plumeria and suits container culture.

directions: Plant cuttings in extremely well-drained, sandy soil in full sun. Dwarf Singapore Pink is a compact-growing form of the evergreen-leaning Plumeria obtusa group, bearing clusters of soft pink-blushed white flowers with a sweet, classic frangipani fragrance on a plant that stays noticeably smaller and more branched than standard tree-form plumeria, making it well suited to container culture and smaller gardens. It tends to hold its glossy, rounded leaves through mild winters rather than dropping them completely the way the deciduous rubra-type plumerias do. Water sparingly and allow soil to dry between waterings, since overwatering in cool weather is the most common cause of stem and root rot; where winters bring hard freezes, grow it in a container that can be moved to a protected spot.

planting.note: Allow cuttings to dry and callus for 1-2 weeks before planting in extremely well-drained, sandy soil in full sun; Mai Tai is prized among collectors for its multi-toned flower color.

directions: Plant cuttings in extremely well-drained, sandy soil in full sun. Mai Tai is a plumeria cultivar bearing large flowers that blend pink, yellow, and white across each petal in a soft, sunset-like gradient, carrying the strong, sweet, classic plumeria fragrance the genus is known for. Its multi-toned coloring and full flower form have made it a favorite among plumeria collectors and lei makers alike. Like other deciduous plumeria, it drops its leaves and rests through the cool season, resuming growth and bloom as temperatures warm in spring. Water sparingly, especially during winter dormancy, since overwatering in cool weather quickly causes stem and root rot; protect from any frost, since plumeria has no cold tolerance.

planting.note: Allow cuttings to dry and callus for 1-2 weeks before planting in extremely well-drained, sandy soil in full sun.

directions: Plant cuttings in extremely well-drained, sandy soil in full sun. Aztec Gold is a plumeria cultivar bearing rich, deep golden-yellow flowers with only a thin white edge at the petal tips, a bolder, more saturated gold than the pale yellow-centered blooms of many other plumeria, carrying the strong, sweet, classic frangipani fragrance. Like other deciduous plumeria, it drops its leaves and rests through the cool season before flushing new growth and flowers as temperatures warm. Water sparingly, especially during winter dormancy, since overwatering in cool weather quickly leads to stem and root rot; protect from any frost, since plumeria has no cold tolerance and is grown as a container plant well outside zone 10 and warmer.

planting.note: Plant container plants after the last frost in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral, lean soil in full sun; bougainvilleas bloom most prolifically under slight water and fertilizer stress. Rosenka's compact, mounding habit suits containers and hanging baskets.

directions: Plant in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral, lean soil in full sun. Rosenka is a compact, dwarf bougainvillea whose bracts open a warm peachy-gold and age to deep rose-pink, so a single plant carries both colors at once as older and newer bracts mix, giving it a shifting, two-toned display unlike single-color cultivars. Its low, mounding, semi-trailing habit makes it well suited to containers, hanging baskets, and low borders where the larger, more rampant bougainvillea vines would be unmanageable. As with other bougainvillea, avoid overwatering and excess nitrogen fertilizer, both of which push leafy growth at the expense of bract production; let soil dry between waterings for the heaviest bloom.

planting.note: Plant container plants after the last frost in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral, lean soil in full sun; bougainvilleas bloom most prolifically under slight water and fertilizer stress. Helen Johnson's compact, small-leaved habit is popular for bonsai and container training.

directions: Plant in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral, lean soil in full sun. Helen Johnson is a naturally dwarf bougainvillea with small leaves and thornless-looking fine branching relative to standard bougainvillea, producing an abundance of bright magenta-pink bracts on a compact plant that stays manageable in a pot without heavy pruning. Its small scale and dense branching structure have made it a favorite subject for bonsai training as well as a straightforward container or low-hedge plant for gardeners who want bougainvillea color without a sprawling vine. As with other bougainvillea, avoid overwatering and excess nitrogen fertilizer, both of which push leafy growth at the expense of bract production.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs after the last frost in acidic, moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Nora Grant blooms most heavily in full sun and needs consistently warm temperatures.

directions: Plant in acidic, moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade. Nora Grant is a widely grown ixora cultivar bearing large, rounded clusters of soft coral-pink, star-shaped flowers almost continuously through the warm season, held above glossy, leathery, deep green foliage on a dense, upright shrub. It is one of the more cold-tolerant and larger-growing ixora cultivars, making it a popular flowering hedge or specimen shrub in warm-climate landscapes where its steady bloom provides season-long color with minimal care. Keep soil consistently moist but well drained, feed with an acid-forming fertilizer to prevent the yellowing that ixora shows in alkaline soil, and protect from any frost, since it has little cold tolerance.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs after the last frost in acidic, moist, well-drained soil in full sun; Maui blooms most heavily in full sun and needs consistently warm temperatures.

directions: Plant in acidic, moist, well-drained soil in full sun. Maui is a compact ixora cultivar with smaller leaves and a lower, denser habit than standard ixora shrubs, producing rounded clusters of bright yellow-orange, star-shaped flowers over a long warm-season bloom period. Its naturally compact, tidy form needs little pruning to stay dense and full, making it a popular low hedge, foundation planting, or container shrub where a smaller-scale flowering shrub is wanted. Keep soil consistently moist but well drained, feed with an acid-forming fertilizer to prevent the yellowing that ixora shows in alkaline soil, and protect from any frost, since it has little cold tolerance.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs after the last frost in acidic, moist, well-drained soil in full sun; Super King blooms most heavily in full sun and needs consistently warm temperatures.

directions: Plant in acidic, moist, well-drained soil in full sun. Super King is an ixora cultivar bred for unusually large flower clusters and individual florets, producing bold, rounded heads of vivid red, star-shaped flowers noticeably bigger than those of standard ixora cultivars, held above large, glossy, deep green leaves on a vigorous upright shrub. Its bold flower size and rich color make it a strong specimen or accent shrub where a smaller-flowered ixora would read as too fine-textured. Keep soil consistently moist but well drained, feed with an acid-forming fertilizer to prevent the yellowing that ixora shows in alkaline soil, and protect from any frost, since it has little cold tolerance.
